ingredients: 1/3 cup cup orange juice, plus orange slices for garnish kosher salt
name: Glazed Pork Tenderloin
recipe: Preheat oven to 400º and grease a large baking sheet. Arrange tenderloin on the pan with orange slices under the edges and season generously with salt and pepper.
In a medium saucepan, bring orange juice, brown sugar, garlic, and Italian seasoning to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until reduced by half, 5 to 7 minutes. Pour mixture over pork.
Bake for 25 minutes, then switch to broil and cook 5 minutes more. Slice and serve immediately.

ingredients: 2 large pieces of pita (large flat Syrian bread)
Olive oil (to spray or brush on liners)
name: Green Eggs and Pita
recipe: Wisk eggs, milk and salt
Stir in feta and spinach
Line muffin pan with paper or silicone liners and spray or brush oil on the liners
Slice bread into 1/8 th pieces and place in the muffin pan liners
Top pita in liners about ¾ of the way with egg batter
Add ~ 1 T of labne to the middle of the egg batter
Bake for 25 minutes
Top with preferred topping(s); zaatar, sumac, parsley

ingredients: 4 large baking potatoes (thoroughly washed and dried)
⅓ cup flat leafed parsley, finely chopped
1 tablespoon fresh or pickled jalapeno, minced
name: Chimichurri Hasselback Potatoes
recipe: Combine all ingredients from the olive oil to the kosher salt in a small bowl, cover and let sit at room temperature for at least 2 hours to allow flavors to develop.
When ready to bake the potatoes, preheat the oven to 425F/218C.

Slice each potato at ¼ inch intervals, three quarters of the way though (be careful not to fully cut through the bottom of the potato). Place on a baking sheet or pan and drizzle each potatoes with 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Bake for 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until browned and cooked throughout.
Remove potatoes from the oven and top each one generously with the chimichurri.

ingredients: ¾ cup (180 ml) whole milk, (low-fat works too)
1 cup (40 g) finely chopped fresh spinach
½ cup (60 g) chopped onion, about half a large onion
1 cup (145 g or 5 oz) diced cooked ham
name: Swiss cheese Muffin Tin Quiche
recipe: Roll out pie crusts and use a 4-inch round cookie cutter to cut circles (3.5-inch round works too). Lightly grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with the butter. Place dough circles in muffin tin and press gently into the bottom and sides of each cup. Place muffin tin in the freezer while preparing the filling. Place any leftover pie dough in the refrigerator before making the next batch.
Preheat oven to 375° F.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, cream, salt, pepper and cayenne (if using). Stir in spinach, onion, ham and cheese.
Remove muffin tin from the freezer and fill each cup with egg filling. Leave about ¼-inch of room at the top as the filling will puff up a little as it bakes.

Bake mini quiches at 375° F for 25 to 30 minutes or until the centers are set and the edges are starting to brown. Let the quiches cool in the pan for 10 minutes before removing them and serving warm.

ingredients: 25 - 30 ripe Plum or Roma tomatoes (should have a little give)
name: Panes con Pollo
recipe: Spatchcock the chicken and season it all over with salt. Leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight.
For the Sauce: Soak the annatto seeds in boiling water. Preheat the oven to 450° F. Char the tomatoes, onions and garlic under a broiler turning the tomatoes occasionally until all sides are charred.

In a dry pan toast the pepitas over medium- low heat until they start to take on a golden color ~ 5-10 minutes. Then add the sesame seeds and toast them until they take on a golden color as well. Finally about 30 seconds - 1 minute before the seeds are done toasting, add the cumin, all spice, and bay leaves. Toast until aromatic.

Blend the tomatoes, onions, garlic, pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, cumin, all spice, bay leaves and annatto seeds together. Place the mixture into a large pot and simmer over low heat. If the mixture is/gets too thick, loosen it up with water or chicken stock.
While the mixture simmers, roast the chicken for about 40 minutes - 1 hour until the internal temperature of the breast is 145-150° F and the joint between the thigh and body reads 175° F.
Strain the sauce, discarding the solids. Add the roast chicken juices and season to taste. Optionally add a chunk of dark chocolate at this point.
For the Curtido: While the sauce is simmering and the chicken is roasting, make the curtido. Place onions, carrots, and cabbage in a heat proof bowl and sprinkle a generous amount of salt over them.

Heat equal parts vinegar and water to a rolling boil then pour over the vegetable. Allow to cool on the counter until the vegetables have softened, stirring occasionally. To assemble: Cut the bread in half part way. Lay down a lettuce leaf. Ladle a generous portion of sauce over the lettuce. Layer some sliced chicken. Top with the curtido. Several sprigs of water cress. Add any other desired toppings (radish, cucumber spears, bell pepper). Finally ladle on another helping of sauce. EAT!

ingredients: ½ medium white onion, finely chopped
2 (15-ounce) cans pinto, kidney or black beans, rinsed
1 chipotle pepper in adobo, finely chopped, plus 2 tablespoons adobo sauce, or 1 tablespoon chili powder
Pico de gallo and Cotija cheese, for serving (optional)
name: Refried Beans
recipe: In a large (preferably cast-iron) skillet, heat oil over medium. Cook onion, garlic and bacon, stirring occasionally, until the fat has rendered, the bacon is crispy and the onion is browned and tender, 8 to 10 minutes.

Increase heat to medium-high and add beans, chipotle and adobo sauce, and ⅔ cup water. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid has slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Using a potato masher, smash beans until the mixture is thick and creamy. Remove from heat, taste and season with salt, if necessary. Let cool slightly; the refried beans will thicken as they sit. Serve with pico de gallo and Cotija cheese, if desired.

ingredients: 1 tablespoon red wine vinegar or white wine vinegar
1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt, or more to taste
name: Homemade Mayo
recipe: Add egg to the small bowl of a food processor and process for 20 seconds. Add the mustard, vinegar, and salt. Process for another 20 seconds.

Scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl, turn the food processor on then begin to slowly add the oil in tiny drops until about a quarter of the oil has been added (this is critical for proper emulsification).

When you notice that the mixture is beginning to thicken and emulsify, you can be a little less strict. With the processor on, continue to add it slowly, but increase to a very thin stream instead of drops of oil.
When all of the oil has been added, scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl and process for an extra 10 seconds. Taste mayonnaise for seasoning then add salt, lemon juice or extra vinegar to taste.

ingredients: 3 Tbsp lime juice or lemon juice
Approx. 6 Tbsp water (depending on desired consistency)
name: Lentil Hummus
recipe: First, follow the package instructions to cook the lentils in a medium saucepan until tender. For more flavor, cook them in vegetable stock with 1-2 bay leaves.

Then, drain and transfer the lentils and all the remaining ingredients (except the parsley) to a blender and blend until the dip is smooth and creamy. Add the water, one tablespoon at a time, until it reaches your desired consistency.
Taste the dip and adjust any of the elements to your liking. i.e., more salt or pepper, lemon/lime juice, garlic, cumin, etc.
Finally, transfer the lentil hummus to a serving dish and garnish with fresh parsley and an optional drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil. Serve with naan, crackers, or vegetable sticks, and enjoy!

name: Fried Plantains
recipe: Peel the plantains and cut into thick slices.
Fry once until they soften.
Remove and flatten with a cup or press.
Fry again until golden and crispy.
Drain, add salt, and serve hot.

ingredients: 1/4 cup packed cilantro leaves and tender stems
2 tablespoons fresh lime juice, plus more if needed
name: Kosher salt Salsa Roja
recipe: Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high heat. Add the tomatoes, garlic, chiles and onion and cook, turning occasionally, until charred on all sides, about 3 minutes for the garlic, 4 to 5 minutes for the chiles, 6 to 8 minutes for the onion and 8 to 10 minutes for the tomatoes. Transfer to a plate to cool. When cool enough to handle, peel the garlic.

Add the tomatoes, garlic, chiles, onion, cilantro, lime juice and 1 tablespoon salt to a blender and puree on low speed, stopping to scrape the sides and bottom to ensure an even texture, until the salsa is almost smooth but some small pieces remain. Season with salt and more lime juice if needed.

ingredients: 2 to 4 jalapeño or serrano chiles, to taste, coarsely chopped (and seeded, if you would like a milder salsa)
¼ cup chopped white or yellow onion, soaked for 5 minutes in cold water, drained and rinsed
name: Salt to taste Salsa Verde
recipe: Heat broiler, positioning a rack at the highest setting under the heat. Cover a baking sheet with foil and place tomatillos on top, stem side down. Broil 2 to 5 minutes, until charred on one side. Turn tomatillos over and broil 2 to 5 minutes longer, until charred. Transfer tomatillos to a blender, tipping in any juice that may have accumulated on the foil.

Add chiles, onions, garlic (if using), cilantro and ¼ cup water to blender and blend to a coarse purée. Transfer to a bowl and thin out as desired with water. Taste and adjust salt. Set aside for at least 30 minutes before serving, to allow the flavors to develop.

ingredients: 2 tablespoons olive oil; add more for extra richness
name: Tofu Ricotta
recipe: Drain the tofu (there is no need to press it dry), break it up with your hands, and place it, along with the other ingredients, in a food processor.
Pulse until well combined and coarsely ground, but not smooth.

name: Biscuits
recipe: Cut butter into small pieces and set aside in the refrigerator.
Mix flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Add butter to the flour mixture and blend with your hands until small pea size pieces.
Add buttermilk and (being careful not to overwork) form into a soft, slightly moist dough. (If adding chives, add now).
Add more buttermilk if necessary.
Flatten to 3/4 inch thickness and cut into rounds.
Bruch the tops with cream and dust with sugar or cheese.
Bake at 375 on two sheet pans for +/- 16 minutes.

ingredients: 1/4 cup (60ml) tahini, try our homemade tahini recipe
name: Baba Ganoush
recipe: Adjust an oven rack to the middle position and turn the broiler on (high heat). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Place the eggplants on the baking sheet and prick them in several places using a fork (this helps steam escape while the eggplants roast).
Broil eggplants for 2 minutes on all sides. The skin will darken a little and begin to smell smoky, adding flavor to the dip.
Turn the broiler off, but do not remove the eggplants from the oven.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roast the eggplants until very soft, 25 to 30 minutes. Cool them for 10 to 15 minutes or until you can easily handle them.
While the eggplants roast, combine the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside so the flavors meld.
Split the roasted eggplants, drain excess liquid, scrape out the flesh, and add to the tahini mixture. (Discard excess liquid and skins).
Mash the roasted eggplant into the tahini mixture with a fork until somewhat smooth, with some texture remaining.
Cool to room temperature, stir in parsley, and drizzle the top with olive oil.

ingredients: ¼ cup canola or vegetable oil
name: Honey Cornbread
recipe: Preheat Oven to 400 degrees.
In a saute’ pan, melt butter over medium heat and wait until butter begins to brown. Be careful not to burn. Remove from heat and cool.

In a large bowl, whisk together all- purpose flour, corn meal, baking powder and sugar until well mixed. In a separate medium sized bowl, whisk together buttermilk, honey, eggs, vanilla extract, oil, and cooled browned butter.
Slowly add wet mixture to dry mixture and mix together until well combined.
Coat cast iron skillet with shortening until fully covered. Place cast iron skillet in preheated oven for 4-5 minutes.
Remove cast iron skillet from oven and add cornbread mixture to skillet. Place back in oven for 22-25 minutes until cornbread is done. Remove from oven and serve.

ingredients: 1 teaspoon paprika (use smoked paprika, if desired)
name: Chili Seasoning
recipe: Mix all ingredients together in a small bowl or jar. Store in a small airtight container.
After cooking meat and vegetables for chili, stir in spice mix and toast for 1-2 minutes before adding liquid ingredients to chili.

name: Gravy
recipe: Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat, then add onions. Cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are translucent, about 5 minutes. Sprinkle the flour on the onions, stirring constantly, and cook until flour is golden to brown. Adjust heat so mixture does not burn.
Gradually whisk in 4 cups stock until mixture thickens and is smooth. If it is too thick, add liquid. Cool, cover and chill.
When ready to serve, reheat mixture over low heat, stirring. Scrape bottom of turkey pan and add drippings or giblets to gravy. Taste and adjust seasoning, then serve.

name: Cashew Queso
recipe: Blend until smooth.

name: Cashew Cesar
recipe: Blend until smooth.

name: Sriracha Water Salt Spicy Peanut Sauce
recipe: Blend until smooth.

ingredients: 4 cups (packed) radish tops, (4 good handfuls) washed and dried
1/2 cup sliced or slivered almonds, coarsely chopped macadamia nuts, pistachios or pine nuts
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
name: Radish Top Pesto
recipe: Combine all ingredients in a food processor or blender. Process until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.

ingredients: use: himalayan salt, sea salt, flakey salt, iodized salt, coarse salt
Your preferred pickling vegetable: cucumbers, carrots, peppers, etc.
Spices (whole seed, not powdered): Mustard , bay leaf, black peppercorns, coriander
For quick pickle brine:  ½ cup vinegar
name: Homemade Pickles
portions: Pickling or pure salt - do not
recipe: Method 1: Quick pickle -
Cut vegetables to desired size. Add vegetables and aromatic flavorings into a clean heat-proof jar.
Heat a sauce pan with ½ cup vinegar, 1 teaspoon salt, 2 teaspoons sugar, and spice seeds until simmering and sugar dissolves.
Pour simmering liquid over the vegetables. Stir and cover.
Allow to cool, then store in the fridge for up to 1 month.
Method 2: Lacto-fermented pickles -
Cut vegetables to desired size. Add vegetables flavorings into a clean heat-proof jar. Place jar with veggies on a kitchen scale, and hit the tare button to zero out (scale should read 0).

Pour in water until veggies are completely covered. Record the weight of the water, and calculate 4% of that weight. That is the amount of salt you will add to the water. For example, if the water weighs 100 grams, 4% would be 4 grams of salt.
Once the salt, water, veggies, and flavorings are combined, lightly screw on the jar’s lid and shake to dissolve the salt.

Double check that the veggies are completely submerged in the liquid. If not, add something to weigh down the veggies like a pickling weight or a plastic bag filled with water. Anything above the water line could spoil the batch.
Place at room temperature out of direct sunlight for 2-5 days. Once the pickles taste as desired, store in the fridge and eat within 3 months.

ingredients: 12 oz fettuccine pasta (cooked according to package instructions)
name: Alfredo Sauce
recipe: Melt the butter over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and sauté for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the heavy cream, stirring frequently, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low and whisk in the Parmesan cheese until smooth.
Season with the remaining salt, black pepper, and nutmeg (if using). Simmer for another 2-3 minutes until thickened.
Add the cooked fettuccine pasta to the sauce and toss to coat evenly.

ingredients: ¼ to ½ cup olive oil
name: Easy Red Sauce
recipe: Add whole tomatoes to a food processor and blend until slightly chunky.
Add olive oil to the bottom of a cold sauce pan. Add garlic and onion.
Heat from cold for about 3-4 minutes so it doesn’t scald. This will add the flavor to the oil.
Add fresh basil and cook for 1 minute.
Add blended tomatoes, and add salt and pepper to taste.

Bring to a simmer and cook to your desired taste. If you like a fresher sauce, cook for a short amount of time (5-15 minutes). If you like a sweeter sauce, cook for longer (15 minutes - 1 hour). If the sauce remains too acidic, add a pinch of sugar.

ingredients: ½ teaspoon cracked black pepper - or 1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
name: Greek Yogurt Ranch Dip
recipe: Combine all ingredients in a blender or food processor and pulse until smooth.
Taste, add salt and pepper to taste and water to thin to desired consistency. (Add more water for a salad dressing, less if using as a dip)
Chill until ready to serve. Store covered tightly and chilled up to 1 week.

name: Pizza sauce
recipe: Into a high sided container add crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, salt, sugar, basil, oregano, chili flake, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Spin with immersion blender to break down to smooth, but still has texture.

name: Pizza dough
recipe: Cover the bowl with a lid and let the dough ferment on the counter for 30 minutes.

Wet your hand to prevent sticking, and perform a series of strength-building folds. To do this, grab a corner of the dough, stretch it out gently, and fold it back over itself. Repeat this process 4-5 times around different parts of the dough.

After folding, flip the dough so the seams are underneath. Shape the dough into a tight ball by rounding it up from one side to the other while tucking under to create tension. Cover and let sit at room temperature for 60 minutes.
After the total fermentation time of 90 minutes, turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. 7. Divide into four equal pieces, each weighing about 280g.
Shape by folding the sides inwards and turn 90 degrees to repeat, then flip over and roll into a ball to strengthen further.
Spray a baking tray with olive oil and place the pre-shaped dough balls on it. Cover and let them rest for 15 minutes to relax before pressing the dough out into a pizza and topping

Mix warm water with olive oil, yeast, salt, and sugar then use a sturdy spook to gradually add 680g (about 5 1/3 cups) of all-purpose flour to the bowl and combine until flour has hydrated and has formed into a clump of dough.
At this point, switch to mixing using your soaking wet hand. Grab and squeeze the dough repeatedly until ingredients are fully incorporated and dough is homogenous.

name: Salpicón Fruit Punch
recipe: Cut all the fruits into small cubes.
In a large bowl, mix all the fruits together.
Stir gently and chill (with ice or refrigeration).
Serve in cups with a spoon.

ingredients: 2 ounces of rose and tulsi blend
name: Garlic and Rosemary Oxymel
recipe: Place rose and tulsi in 1 pint jar and cover with vinegar. Seal the jar with parchment and non-reactive lid, label and let sit in a cool dry area, shaking the jar daily. Strain vinegar through a fine-mesh sieve, swirl in honey until dissolved; label and store in the refrigerator for up to a year.

ingredients: 1 tablespoon fresh chopped ginger (or more less to taste)
2 cinnamon sticks orange/lemon rinds (from above recipe) cardamom pods (optional)
name: Ginger shots
recipe: Steep all ingredients together in hot water (not quite boiling) for 2-5 minutes. Enjoy with honey or milk.

ingredients: 1 tablespoon zested? orange peel juice of half an orange cinnamon stick (optional) honey, agave or panela
name: Rosehip Wellness Syrup
recipe: While the rosehip decoction is cooling, set up your filtration station. Use a large glass bowl for filtration. Set a fine mesh strainer up to rest on top of the bowl. Next, measure and cut enough cheesecloth to line the strainer twice (a double layer of muslin). Once the muslin is lining the mesh strainer, confidently and carefully pour the decoction through the strainer. Return the remaining rosehips pulp to the saucepan, add a cup of water, cover, and place the pan back over medium-high heat.

Repeat the process using clean cheesecloth to strain the rosehip pulp into the bowl, using a wooden or silicone spatula to press liquid from the pulp, and allow to cool for about 5-10 minutes. Pour the cooled reduction back into a clean pan, stir the honey (sweetener of choice) into the pan on the stove at low heat. Stir continuously until the honey and reduction are fully combined. Once the honey and reduction are fully combined, allow to cool completely.
Pour your rosehip syrup into the pint- sized mason jars. Place a label on the mason jar, and store in the refrigerator. Once the jar is open, syrup should be used within one month.

In a small saucepan, combine rosehips with 2 cups of water and allow to sit for 30 minutes at room temperature. Cover the saucepan, place on the stove over medium-high heat, and bring to a boil; then turn the burner low to simmer for 30 minutes; remove the pan from burner, and allow the decoction to cool a bit before filtering.

name: Electuary
recipe: Mix two teaspoons of ginger, turmeric cinnamon and clove
Sprinkle black pepper on turmeric and cover with honey, about a 1/3 to 1/2 cup into a glass jar
Blend with a spoon or spatula until well blended.

Store on your counter and use as a tea by adding water and lemon to about a spoonful, to your taste. Sometimes just a spoonful is a warming sweet treat, golden candy. Good for inflammation, pain relief and overall immune support.

ingredients: 1 small pc ginger, chopped or grated
name: Soothing Tea
recipe: In a small pot, bring water to a boil. Add in ginger, turmeric and garlic and simmer until all have softened.
Add in lemon juice and honey.
Strain the tea and drink hot.
When storing, keep ginger, garlic and turmeric in the tea, add in a slice of lemon if desired.

ingredients: Veggie (optional but recommended): ½–1 cup (spinach, beet powder,  goji, elderberry)
Protein/Fat Boost: 1–2 tbsp (nut butter, seeds, or hemp or whey protein powder)
name: Greenya Colada Smoothie
recipe: Blend and enjoy!

ingredients: Nuts/Seeds: 1 cup (almonds, cashews, brazil nuts, hazelnuts, or sunflower seeds)
Sweetener (optional): 1–2 tbsp (maple syrup, or agave) or 1 date
Flavor Enhancer (optional): pinch of salt, vanilla extract, or cinnamon
Optional Add-ins: 1–2 tbsp (cacao nibs, protein powder, or tumeric)
name: Nut Mylk
recipe: Soak nuts 4–12 hrs
Pour off the soaking water and rinse the nuts with fresh water.
Blend with water and add flavors.
Strain through a nut milk bag or fine mesh strainer.
Enjoy!

ingredients: 1 cup of milk (dairy or non- dairy)
½ cup fresh or frozen banana
½ orange (peeled and inner membrane removed)
name: Spinach Mango and Mint Smoothie
recipe: Blend all ingredients until completely smooth.

name: Frozen Mint Lemonade
recipe: BLEND UNTIL SMOOTH. ENJOY!

ingredients: 1 teaspoon espresso powder or instant espresso*
1/3 cup (80ml) vegetable or canola oil (or melted coconut oil)
1/2 cup (120ml) buttermilk, at room temperature* chocolate buttercream and sprinkles for decorating
name: Chocolate Cupcakes with Icing
recipe: Preheat the oven to 350°F (177°C). Line a 12- count muffin pan with cupcake liners. Line a second pan with 2 liners—this recipe makes about 14 cupcakes. Set aside.

Whisk the flour, cocoa powder, espresso powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl until thoroughly combined. Set aside. In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, granulated sugar, brown sugar, oil, and vanilla together until completely smooth. Pour half of the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Then half of the buttermilk. Gently whisk for a few seconds. Repeat with the remaining wet ingredients and buttermilk. Stir until *just* combined; do not overmix. The batter will be thin.

Pour or spoon the batter into the liners. Fill only halfway (this is imperative! only halfway!) to avoid spilling over the sides or sinking. Bake for 18-21 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Allow to cool completely before frosting.

Frost cooled cupcakes with chocolate buttercream. You can swipe the frosting on with an icing knife or use a piping tip such as Wilton 1M. Leftover cupcakes keep well covered tightly in the refrigerator for 3 days. I recommend a cupcake carrier for storing and transporting decorated cupcakes.

name: Healthier strawberry cupcakes
recipe: Optional: You can make your own oat flour by putting whole oats in a blender or food processor and blending into a light powder.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Mix oat flour, all purpose flour, salt, baking soda, cinnamon, and sugar in a large bowl.
If your dates have pits, remove them.
In a blender, add vanilla, oil, dates, fruit puree, and banana (if using). Blend until smooth. Mix in eggs.
Pour blended wet ingredients and sliced strawberries into the bowl with dry ingredients and mix by hand until incorporated.
Line a muffin tin with muffin liners, spray lightly with oil, or brush with melted butter so muffins don’t stick. Pour batter into muffin tins until each cup is ¾ full.
Bake for 20-25 minutes.

ingredients: 3 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for surface
1/2 cup (1 stick) cold butter, cut into cubes
1 cup fruit, such as raspberries, blueberries, blackberries, or a mix (chopped, if large)
1 cup heavy cream, plus more for brushing
name: Fruit scones
recipe: Preheat oven to 400° and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugars, baking powder, and salt. Add butter and, using a pastry cutter or your hands, cut butter into flour until the size of peas. Add fruit and toss to coat.

Make a well in mixture and add eggs and heavy cream. Mix with your hands until just combined. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and pat into an 8" round. Cut into 8 triangles and place on prepared baking sheet. (At this point, you can freeze the scones if you like, for later.)
Brush with heavy cream and sprinkle with coarse sugar. Bake until lightly golden, 20 to 22 minutes. (Add another 5 to 10 minutes if baking from frozen.)
Let cool 5 minutes on baking sheet, then transfer the scones to a rack to cool completely.

ingredients: 1 package (3.4 ounces) instant lemon pudding mix
1 tablespoon white grape juice or water
Optional: Whipped topping and additional strawberries
name: Strawberry Lemon Trifle
recipe: In a large bowl, beat cream cheese and yogurt. Add the milk, pudding mix and lemon zest; beat until smooth. In a blender, process 1/2 cup strawberries and grape juice until blended.

Cut cake into 1-in. cubes; place a third in a trifle bowl or 3-qt. serving bowl. Top with a third of the pudding mixture and half of the remaining strawberries. Drizzle with half of the strawberry sauce. Repeat all layers. Top with remaining cake and pudding mixture. If desired, garnish with whipped topping and additional strawberries. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

ingredients: 6 large or 7 medium peaches, thinly sliced
¼ cup melted coconut oil or unsalted butter
name: Peach Cobbler
recipe: Preheat the oven to 400°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with coconut oil.
Layer the peaches into the bottom of the baking dish and drizzle the lemon juice over the peaches.

In a medium bowl, mix the flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt. Add the coconut oil and vanilla and combine until the mixture forms a crumbly dough. Sprinkle over the peaches and bake for 30 minutes, or until the mixture is just lightly browned on top and the peaches are juicy.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

name: Hojaldras pastries
recipe: Mix flour, salt, sugar, eggs, and milk until forming a smooth dough.
Let rest for 10 minutes.
Roll out the dough and cut into squares or strips.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown.
Remove and sprinkle with powdered sugar.

ingredients: 3 ripe medium bananas, mashed, about 1 ¼ cups
5 tablespoons (70g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
name: Banana Muffins
recipe: Heat oven to 350°F (177°C). Line muffin cups with paper liners. This recipe makes 12 regular-sized muffins.
Whisk the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the melted butter, mashed banana, egg, and vanilla until blended.
Stir the banana mixture into the dry ingredients until you no longer see streaks of flour.
Stir in the chocolate chips.
Fill muffin cups 3/4 full. Bake until a toothpick can be inserted and comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool on a wire rack.

ingredients: Diplomat cream: pastry cream mixed with whipped cream
Fruit mousse: mix spoon sweets/compote into your diplomat cream
name: Choux Pastry
recipe: In a pot, bring the butter, water, sugar, and salt to a boil.
Once the butter is fully melted, add the flour and mix on the heat with a wooden spoon. Mix until it comes together into a uniform dough that pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Take off of the heat and transfer to the bowl of an electric mixer. Mix with the paddle attachment until the steam dissipates. Alternatively, you can do this by hand with the same wooden spoon.

Slowly add the eggs 2 at a time, mixing after each addition. Use a rubber spatula to scrape the bowl well and make sure that you dough is completely smooth. If you are making gougeres, now would be the time to mix in the cheese.
Transfer to piping bags and put in the fridge to cool.
Pipe onto parchment lined sheet pans. If you have a convection oven, glue down the sides of the parchment lined with a little bit of dough before piping.
Bake at 375 for 20 minutes, until golden brown. It is very important to not open the oven early or the buns might deflate!
Let cool before filling them.

name: Pastry Cream
recipe: In a medium sized bowl, mix together half of the sugar with the cornstarch.
In a pot, bring the milk, salt, and other half of the sugar to a boil.
While you are waiting for the milk to boil, whisk the egg yolks into the cornstarch mix.
When the milk boils, slowly stream it into the egg yolk mix while whisking continuously.
(This is called “tempering the eggs”). Once it is all mixed, return it to the pot and cook on
medium high heat, stirring constantly. You don’t want the bottom to burn before it is all
cooked. It will get thicker as it cooks. You want to cook the cornstarch completely
(around 3 min). When it’s ready, take it oﬀ of the heat.
Whisk in the butter and vanilla extract.
For an extra smooth texture, strain through a fine mesh strainer.
Scoop into whatever container you are going to store it in and press plastic wrap into the
urface before putting it in the fridge to chill. This prevents a skin from forming on the top.
*The pastry cream can be stored in the fridge for up to 5 days

ingredients: ½ cup toﬀee bits (or other dry mix-in of your choice)
1½ cups (216 g) chocolate, cut into small pieces
name: Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipe: Add the dark brown sugar and the granulated sugar to the browned butter. Whisk until incorporated, about 1 minute. Add the room temperature eggs and vanilla extract. Whisk until the mixture lightens and begins to thicken, about 1 minute.

Switch to a rubber spatula or wooden spoon. Add the dry ingredients and your mix-ins (toﬀee, chocolate, whatever your heart desires). Mix just to combine. Cover and let the dough sit in the mixing bowl at room temperature at least 30 minutes to allow the flour to hydrate. The dough will look very loose at first, but will thicken as it sits.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 375°. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Using a 1-oz. ice cream scoop, portion out balls of dough and place on prepared baking sheet, spacing about 3" apart (you can also form dough into ping pong–size balls with your hands). Do not flatten; cookies will spread as they bake.

Bake cookies until edges are golden brown and firm but centers are still soft, 9–11 minutes. Let cool on baking sheets 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack and let cool completely. Repeat with remaining dough, using a cool baking sheet lined with fresh parchment paper.
*The cookie dough can be made 3 days ahead; cover and chill in the refrigerator— or freeze for up to 3 months. Let dough come to room temperature before baking

In a medium saucepan over medium heat, cook the butter, stirring often, until it foams and starts to get little brown bits, 5–8 minutes. Scrape into a large, heat proof bowl and let cool slightly, until cool enough to touch, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the all-purpose flour, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.

name: Hummingbird Cupcakes
recipe: Toast the pecans. Preheat the oven to 315F
Whisk together the dries.
Using the paddle attachment on a stand mixer or using a hand mixer, combine the eggs, oil, sugars and extract.
Add the fruit.
Add the dries and the pecans. Be careful not to overmix. Portion with a scoop into a sprayed muffin pans.
Give it a good tap to make sure the surface is flat.
Bake at 315 degrees F for 18-20 minutes

name: Cream Cheese Frosting
recipe: Soften the cream cheese and the butter in the microwave.
Cream together using a kitchen aid (with the paddle attachment) or hand held electric mixer.

Add half the powdered sugar, mix until incorporated. Using a rubber spatula, scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl well, then add the other half of the sugar. Mix until incorporated then add the vanilla extract and salt. Be careful not to over mix.

name: Sweet Salty Candied Nuts
recipe: Pour the nuts into a big bowl.
Pour the warm corn syrup and sea salt over nuts and toss to coat.
Mix in the powdered sugar until it isn’t white anymore (add more corn syrup if necessary).
Bake 275 for about 10 min, stir, add time if not caramelized enough.

name: Berry Compote
recipe: Mix the fruit with the sugar. Crush with your hands a little to release some juices. Set aside to macerate until most of the sugar is dissolved.
When ready, pour into a pot and add the lemon peel. Boil until it begins to thicken. Do the frozen spoon test. You still want some whole pieces of fruit.
Take off the heat, add the lemon juice and salt. Adjust to taste.

ingredients: ¼ cup (60 g) salted butter melted
½ cup (100 g) brown sugar light or dark (I usually use light) tightly packed
10 pineapple slices patted dry (a 20oz can is typically enough) maraschino cherries
½ cup (115 g) unsalted butter softened to room temperature
½ cup (120 ml) whole milk room temperature preferred
name: Pineapple Upside Down Cake
recipe: Preheat oven to 350F (175C)
Pour melted butter into 9.5-10" pie plate or deep cake pan, make sure it entirely covers the bottom of the pan and use a spoon or spatula to grease the sides of the pan.
Sprinkle brown sugar evenly over butter mixture.  Arrange pineapple slices over the bottom of the pan, slice leftover slices in half and arrange up the sides of the pan.
Place cherries in center of pineapple rings and as desired in empty spaces.  Set aside.
To prepare vanilla cake, beat butter and sugar in medium-sized bowl until creamy and well-combined.
Add eggs, beating one at a time until combined.  Stir in vanilla.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Alternate adding flour and milk to the wet ingredients, starting and ending with flour and mixing until just combined after each addition
Pour batter evenly over prepared cake pan over the pineapple/cherry layer.

Bake on 350F (175C) for 30 minutes.  At the 30 minute mark, loosely cover with foil and continue to bake (still on 350F/175C) for another 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out mostly clean with few crumbs (total cook time for cake will be 45 minutes).
Allow to cool for 10-15 minutes and then carefully invert cake onto serving platter (careful, it will still be very hot!).
Allow to cool before cutting and enjoying, but don’t wait too long as this cake tastes wonderful (best!) warm from the oven!

name: Royal icing
recipe: Using whisk attachment on a stand mixer, whip egg whites with cream of tartar until eggs are frothy and glossy.
Add powdered sugar in 2 batches, scraping the sides between additions, until incorporated.
Add to a piping bag and use to decorate cookies.

name: Sugar Cookies
recipe: Measure the following ingredients together: butter, sugar, and salt; milk, eggs, and vanilla; flour and baking powder.
In a mixer, cream butter, sugar, and salt on medium speed until smooth.
Lower the mix to low speed and slowly add the wets (milk, egg, vanilla) until incorporated.
Add the dries (flour and baking powder) in 2 additions, scraping the bowl in between.
Turn the dough out onto plastic wrap and form dough into a log about 3-4 inches in diameter. Wrap tightly in plastic.
Dough can be stored in the fridge at this point or baked. To bake: preheat oven to 325, and once preheated, bake for 10-11 minutes until the edges just start to brown.

ingredients: 12 large egg whites, at room temperature
name: Angel Food Cake
recipe: In a large bowl using a hand mixer or a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment, whip egg whites and cream of tartar together on medium-low until foamy, about 1 minute. Switch to medium-high and slowly add the 1 cup of sugar you set aside. Whip until soft peaks form, about 5-6 minutes. See photo and video above for a visual. Add the vanilla extract, then beat just until incorporated.

In 3 additions, slowly sift the flour mixture into the egg white mixture using a fine mesh strainer, gently folding with a rubber spatula after each addition. To avoid deflating or a dense cake, don’t add the flour mixture all at once. Sift and very slowly fold in several additions. This is important! Pour and spread batter into an ungreased 9 or 10 inch tube pan. Shimmy the pan on the counter to smooth the surface

Bake the cake until a toothpick inserted comes out clean, about 40-45 minutes. Rotate the pan halfway through baking. The cake will rise up very tall while baking. Remove from the oven, then cool the cake completely upside-down set on a wire rack, about 3 hours. (Upside-down so the bottom of the tube pan is right-side up, see photo and video above.) Once cooled, run a thin knife around the edges and gently tap the pan on the counter until the cake releases.
If desired, dust with confectioners’ sugar. Slice the cake with a sharp serrated knife. Regular knives can easily squish the cake. Serve with whipped cream and fresh berries.
Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
Adjust the oven rack to the lower middle position and preheat oven to 325°F (163°C).

In a food processor or blender, pulse the sugar until fine and powdery. Remove 1 cup and set aside to use in step 3; keep the rest inside the food processor. Add the cake flour and salt to the food processor. Pulse 5-10 times until sugar/flour/salt mixture is aerated and light.

ingredients: 2 tablespoons neutral oil, like canola, plus a teaspoon more
1 packet of active dried yeast, or 7 grams
name: Naan
recipe: Put the flour into a large mixing bowl. Make a well in the middle, and add two tablespoons of the oil to it, along with the yogurt, yeast, sugar, salt and baking powder. Use your fingers to combine the ingredients until they resemble crumbs, and then add the warm milk in splashes, mixing until it comes together into a dough.

Put the dough on a clean, well-floured cutting board. It will be very sticky. Flour your hands, and knead the dough for five minutes or so, then scrape off your hands and knead it again, making it into a round ball. Rub a teaspoon of oil over the exterior of the dough, and place it in a clean mixing bowl. Cover with a dish towel, and place in a warm spot to rise for 60 to 90 minutes, or until it has doubled in size.

Using a knife, divide the dough into 12 pieces. Take each piece, roll it into a ball and flatten it between your palms. Dust the dough with flour, and roll each piece out into an oval of about 5 by 8 inches.

Place a large sauté pan over medium-high heat, and allow it to get hot. When it is, cook one naan in it for 30 to 40 seconds on one side, or until it begins to bubble, then use a spatula to flip it over to cook the other side for about the same amount of time, checking regularly to make sure that it does not burn. Flip the naan one more time, and press on it lightly with your spatula for 10 to 15 seconds, then remove to a warm platter. Repeat with the rest of the dough. (Keep the finished naan in a low oven, or wrap in foil until ready to serve.)

ingredients: 780 grams or 5 ½  cups of bread flour
680 grams or 2 ¾ cups of water
5 grams or 2 teaspoons of instant yeast
110 grams or ½ cup of olive oil
name: Focaccia Bread
recipe: Add about ¼ cup of olive oil to a large bowl and swirl to coat all sides. Place dough in the bowl and cover with a damp towel. Allow to rise for 1-1.5 hours, until doubled in size.

After the dough has doubled in size, stretch the dough gently and fold over itself 2 to 3 times. Then flip the dough over and transfer it onto an oiled baking sheet. Spread a bit of oil on the top of the dough and wrap in plastic warp.
At this point, either place in the fridge for up to 24 hours, or leave on the counter top for 40-55 minutes (until risen and very pillowy).
Half an hour before you plan to bake, preheat your oven to 475 degrees F.

Right before baking, drizzle your focaccia with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Dimple the dough by pressing your fingertips into top and pressing down, repeating all across the dough’s surface.
You can also add any toppings you like to the focaccia. Some examples:
Thin sliced potatoes and rosemary
Roasted garlic and parmesan cheese
Fresh vegetables like bell pepper slices and asparagus
Sliced figs, honey and goat cheese
Bake your focaccia at 475 degrees F for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown. Allow to cool before serving.

Add flour, water, salt, and yeast to a bowl. Mix until you can no longer see or feel the salt or yeast, and all of the flour is damp. The dough is too sticky to knead on the countertop. Instead, knead in the bowl by scooping your hand underneath the dough repeatedly, stretching outward each time. Repeat that scooping motion 5-10 times on one section of the dough, and then turn the bowl and scoop 5-10 at another section of the dough. Continue this for 5-10 minutes, until the dough is smooth and slightly less sticky than when you began.

ingredients: 3/4 cup golden or white granulated sugar
2 large eggs, at room temperature (approx. 55g-60g in shell)
3/4 cup whole milk, at room temperature
1/2 tsp fine salt, or Kosher salt
1 1/2 cups frozen or fresh raspberries, if using frozen do not thaw before adding
name: Raspberry Cake
recipe: Preheat oven to 180ºC (350ºF). Line an 8- inch round baking pan with parchment paper, and set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, add sugar and the eggs. Using electric hand beaters, beat on low-medium speed for 30 seconds until well combined. Scrape down the sides if needed with a spatula.
With the beater running on medium-high speed, slowly drizzle in the olive oil in a slow steady stream to emulsify while beating, about 1 minute in total.
Pour in the milk and vanilla. Beat for 15 seconds until well combined. Scrape down the sides if needed.

Add flour, baking powder, and salt. Beat until incorporated, about 15 seconds, do not over-mix, just until it’s incorporated into a smooth batter and no pockets or streaks of flour remain. Scrape down the sides.
Add the raspberries and fold to incorporate, do not over-mix.
Pour batter into the prepared baking pan. Smoothing out the top. If desired, scatter top with extra raspberries.

Bake for 45-50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the middle, comes out clean or with a few crumbs on it. NOTE: as this has raspberries, the cake is extra moist and takes a little longer to bake than usual.
Remove from the oven and allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a wire rack to cool.
Serve and enjoy!

name: Spanish Flan
recipe: Make the caramel: Heat sugar in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Don't stir - just swirl the pan occasionally until the sugar melts and turns golden amber. Immediately pour into your baking dish(es), coating the bottom and slightly up the sides. Let it harden and crack.
Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C)
Whisk together eggs, milk sweetened condensed milk, vanilla extract, and salt.
Strain the mixture through a fine- mesh sieve and pour carefully into your caramel-lined dish(es)
Set up your water bath: place the flan dishes into a larger baking dish. Fill the outer dish with hot water halfway up the sides of the flan dishes.
Bake the whole water bath and flan dish setup until the center is still jiggly, about 50-60 minutes for one large flan or 25-35 minutes for small flans.

name: Coconut Ice Cream
recipe: Combine cream, coconut milk, and half the sugar. In a saucepan, slowly heat up the mixture to no higher than 180 degrees F.

Separate the egg yolks and put them into a separate bowl. Temper the eggs by adding a small amount of the hot cream mixture while whisking vigorously. Then slowly stream in more of the hot cream mixture, still whisking quickly, until everything is
Cook the custard over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon (about 170-175 degrees F)
Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve and chill in an ice bath.

ingredients: 2 tablespoons Demerara sugar, plus more as needed
4 cups berries, or pitted and sliced stone fruit (peaches, nectarines, apricots, plums), or rhubarb (or use a combination of stone fruit and berries)
1 tablespoon lemon juice or mild vinegar, such as rice wine vinegar or balsamic
1 tablespoon honey, plus more as needed
All-purpose flour, for dusting the work surface
1 (14-ounce) package puff pastry, preferably made with butter, thawed if frozen, but still very cold
Whipped cream, crème fraîche or ice cream, for serving
name: Summer Fruit Tart
recipe: Put a rack in the center of the oven and heat oven to 400 degrees. Line a baking sheet with a silicone liner or parchment paper. Sprinkle 2 tablespoons Demerara sugar in an approximate 10-by-13-inch rectangle in the center of the liner or paper.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together granulated sugar, cornstarch and salt. Add fruit, lemon juice, honey and vanilla. With a rubber spatula or large spoon, mix well, making sure fruit is coated with the cornstarch mixture. Set aside to macerate while rolling out dough.

On a lightly floured surface, roll the cold puff pastry out to form a 10-by-13-inch rectangle. Work quickly, as the pastry becomes sticky as it warms up. Transfer the dough to prepared baking sheet, laying it on top of the Demerara sugar. With a sharp knife, lightly score a ¾-inch border around the edges of the puff pastry, making sure not to cut the pastry all the way through. Using a fork, prick the pastry all over inside the border at 1-inch intervals.

Give the fruit another toss to dissolve any honey that may have clumped. Arrange fruit mixture in an even layer on pastry within the border, pouring the juices from the bowl over the top. Sprinkle the top of the tart, including the fruit and pastry borders, with more Demerara sugar.

Bake until the pastry is puffed and deeply golden and the fruit is tender, about 30 to 40 minutes. Transfer the pan to a wire tack to cool for at least 15 minutes before serving (or up to 4 hours). If the fruit looks dry when the tart comes out of the oven, you can brush it with a little more honey while it’s still warm. Serve with whipped cream, crème fraîche or ice cream.

name: Fruit Bark
recipe: Mash raspberries with a fork, mix raspberries with Greek yogurt and syrup.
Spread mixture on a flat baking pan, on parchment paper.
Add toppings and freeze for a few hours.

ingredients: 2 ½ pounds apples, peeled and cored, then cut into wedges (5 large honeycrisps will do it)
name: Apple pie
recipe: Melt butter in a large skillet set over medium- high heat and add apples to the pan. Stir to coat fruit with butter and cook, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, whisk together the spices, salt and ¾ cup sugar, and sprinkle this over the pan, stirring to combine. Lower heat and cook until apples have started to soften, approximately 5 to 7 minutes.

Sprinkle the flour and cornstarch over the apples and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, another 3 to 5 minutes. Remove pan from heat, add cider vinegar, stir and scrape fruit mixture into a bowl and allow to cool completely. (The fruit mixture will cool faster if spread out on a rimmed baking sheet.)

Place a large baking sheet on the middle rack of oven and preheat to 425. Remove one disc of dough from the refrigerator and, using a pin, roll it out on a lightly floured surface until it is roughly 12 inches in diameter.

Fit this crust into a 9-inch pie plate, trimming it to leave a ½-inch overhang. Place this plate, with the dough, in the freezer. Roll out the remaining dough on a lightly floured surface until it is roughly 10 or 11 inches in diameter.
Remove pie crust from freezer and put the cooled pie filling into it. Cover with remaining dough.
Press the edges together, trim the excess, then crimp the edges with the tines of a fork. Using a sharp knife, cut four or so steam vents in the top of the crust.
Lightly brush the top of the pie with egg wash and sprinkle with remaining tablespoon of sugar.

Place pie in oven and bake on hot baking sheet for 20 minutes, then reduce temperature to 375. Continue to cook until the interior is bubbling and the crust is golden brown, about 30 to 40 minutes more. Remove and allow to cool on a windowsill or kitchen rack, about two hours.

ingredients: 2 cups (about 300g) fresh or frozen mixed berries (do not thaw & see note)
1 Tablespoon (11g) coconut sugar, brown sugar, or granulated sugar
2 and 1/2 cups (213g) old-fashioned whole rolled oats or quick oats
1/4 cup (56g) coconut oil, melted (or use melted butter) for topping: 1/2 cup (64g) sliced or chopped almonds and 1 extra
name: Healthy Berry Streusel Bars
recipe: Bring to a simmer and allow to simmer for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. After 2 minutes, remove pan from the heat and allow to cool completely. The mixture will thicken as it cools. To speed up the cooling process, feel free to cover and refrigerate it after it slightly cools for at least 30 minutes at room temperature. I recommend making the berry filling in advance so it can cool completely. Berry filling can be cold or room temperature when you assemble the bars—you just don’t want it hot or warm.

Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C). Line the bottom and sides of an 8-inch or 9-inch square baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides to lift the bars out. Make the crust/streusel: Pulse the oats in a food processor or blender until they’re slightly broken up. (For whole oats, about 10 pulses. For quick oats, about 5-6 pulses.) Pour into a bowl and stir in the cinnamon, almond butter, maple syrup, applesauce, and melted coconut oil.

Using the back of a flat spatula or a spoon, press about 3/4 of the crust/streusel mixture tightly and firmly down into the pan. Make sure it’s flat and very compact, which helps guarantee the bars will hold their shape. Spread cooled berry filling evenly on top.
For Topping: Mix the sliced almonds into the remaining crust/streusel mixture. Sprinkle all over the top of the berry filling. Sprinkle 1 Tablespoon of oats evenly on top.

Bake for 27-31 minutes or until the topping is lightly browned. Remove from the oven and place on a cooling rack. Allow bars to cool completely. After about 1 hour cooling at room temperature, you can place the pan in the refrigerator to help speed the cooling up. Lift the cooled bars out using the parchment paper overhang on the sides. Cut into squares.

Berry Filling: Whisk the cornstarch and water together until all the cornstarch has dissolved. (I just use a fork to mix—very easy.) Place the cornstarch mixture, berries, maple syrup, and coconut sugar in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Using a rubber spatula, stir the mixture as it cooks. Smash some of the berries against the bottom/sides of the pot as you stir, gently breaking them up.

ingredients: 2 large onions (1½ pounds), halved lengthwise and thinly sliced
1 pint fresh figs (¾ pound), stemmed and cut in half lengthwise
1 ½ ounces Stilton cheese, crumbled (about 6 tablespoons)
name: Rosemary and Stilton
recipe: In a large skillet over low heat, melt butter with oil. Add onions, rosemary and sugar. Cook, tossing occasionally, until onions are limp and golden brown, 30 to 40 minutes. Stir in the vinegar, scraping any browned bits from bottom of pan.

In a small bowl, whisk together the milk and egg until smooth. Stir in the onions. Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Line an 11 by 17-inch baking sheet with parchment paper. On a lightly floured surface, roll out pastry to a 9 by 12-inch rectangle. Transfer to baking sheet.

Use a fork to spread onion mixture evenly over pastry (let excess egg mixture drip back into bowl), leaving a 1-inch border. Arrange figs, cut-side up, in even rows on onion mixture. Scatter cheese and pine nuts over figs. Use a pastry brush to dab edges of tart with egg mixture. Gently fold over edges of tart to form a lip and brush with more egg mixture.
Bake until pastry is puffed and golden, 25 to 30 minutes. Serve, sprinkled with rosemary needles and drizzled with honey, if desired, warm or at room temperature.

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, spooned into measuring cup and leveled-off
name: Pumpkin Bread
recipe: Preheat the oven to 325°F and set an oven rack in the middle position. Generously grease two 8 x 4-inch loaf pans with butter and dust with flour or pan spray
In a medium bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking soda, baking powder, cloves, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Whisk until well combined; set aside.

In a large bowl of an electric mixer, beat the butter and sugar on medium speed until just blended. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Continue beating until very light and fluffy, a few minutes. Beat in the pumpkin. The mixture might look grainy and curdled at this point -- that's okay.
Add the flour mixture and mix on low speed until combined.

Turn the batter into the prepared pans, dividing evenly, and bake for 65 – 75 minutes, or until a cake tester inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the loaves cool in the pans for about 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

ingredients: 2 tbsp Peanut Butter .5 cup Cacao powder .5 cup maple syrup .75 cup Almond Milk (Honey-
name: Chocolate avocado pudding
recipe: Blend to desired consistency

name: Cacao nibs Raw pudding
recipe: Add ingredients to a blender and blend to desired consistency.

ingredients: ⅓ oz vanilla pinch of salt
name: Chia Pudding
recipe: Combine all ingredients and let sit for 2-3 hours minimum, up to 12 hours until pudding reaches desired consistency.

ingredients: 3.5 oz. (100 g) roughly chopped dark chocolate (I used 70% dairy-free dark chocolate)
1 package (12 oz.-340 g) organic silken tofu at room temperature, drained
Toppings: chocolate shavings, raspberries, blackberries, fresh mint
name: Silken Tofu Chocolate Mousse
recipe: Melt the chocolate in the microwave in 30 second intervals, stirring each time, until the chocolate is melted. Set aside to cool at room temperature.
Meanwhile, place the silken tofu and maple syrup in a food processor and blend until very smooth. Add the melted chocolate and blend until well combined.
Scoop the mixture into 3 ramekins or glasses, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
To serve, garnish with chocolate shavings, raspberries, blackberries and a sprig of fresh mint.

ingredients: 1/2 cup grated hard cheese, such as cojita or parmesan sesame seeds, to taste
name: Salvadoran Quesadillas
recipe: Preheat the oven to 350F.

Meanwhile, whisk together the rice flour, baking powder, and salt. Then, in the bowl of a standing mixer, cream the butter with sugar. Drop in the eggs, one at a time, until fully incorporated. Scrape down the sides as needed.
Next beat in the sour cream, cheese, and rice flour mixture until a smooth batter forms.
Spoon into greased muffin tins, filling each one 4/5th of the way up (this batter does not rise much). Sprinkle on the sesame seeds, to taste.
Bake for 15-20 minutes. Let cool to room temperature - it'll taste like a cheesy pound cake. Amazing with a cuppa coffee in the morning.

ingredients: ½ cup hulled mung beans (peeled yellow mung beans, rinse and soak for 1 hour)
¼ cup small sago pearls (tapioca pearls)
4 pandan leaves tied in a knot (can be substituted with 1tsp vanilla extract)
name: Chè Bắp (Vietnamese Sweet Corn Pudding)
recipe: Prep corn: Shuck corn, remove silk, cut kernels off cob. Keep cobs for flavor.

Making the corn/bean stock: In a large pot, combine mung beans, 6 cups water, corn cobs, pandan leaves (if using), and ¼ tsp salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium and cook 10 minutes. Discard corn cobs and pandan leaves.

Add sago & corn: Add sago pearls directly into the boiling mung bean water. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. Add corn kernels and cook another 10–12 minutes, until mung beans are tender, sago is translucent, and corn is cooked.
Sweeten: Stir in sugar and adjust to taste. Simmer 2–3 minutes to dissolve sugar.
Coconut milk topping: In a small saucepan, heat coconut milk with 2 Tbsp sugar and ¼ tsp salt. Mix cornstarch with 1 Tbsp water, stir into coconut milk to thicken slightly.
Serve: Ladle chè into bowls, drizzle with coconut milk topping. Serve warm for comfort, or chilled for a refreshing treat.

ingredients: 3 cups finely shredded zucchini (do not drain)
name: Chocolate Zucchini Muffins
recipe: Preheat oven to 350
Line or spray muffin tin
In a large bowl, combine oil, sugar and vanilla until fully incorporated
Add flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt. Mix until combined. Batter will be dry.
Fold in zucchini by hand. Allow batter to rest for 5 minutes.
Add in chocolate chunks and stir again. Batter should no longer be dry.
Spoon mixture into muffin liners
Bake for 20-25 minutes

ingredients: ¼ cup finely slivered or grated fresh ginger (from a 3-inch piece)
1 pound rhubarb, cut into ½- inch (or slightly smaller) pieces
Handful of toasted pine nuts or chopped pistachio (optional)
name: Fresh Ricotta With Rhubarb and Ginger
recipe: Put sugar, ginger, cardamom and 1 cup water in a nonreactive saucepan or skillet, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Turn heat to low and let syrup simmer for 5 minutes. Do not strain.

Add rhubarb and stir to incorporate syrup, then continue to simmer for another 5 minutes or so. Set aside and let cool. (The rhubarb syrup can be made a day or two in advance, and becomes more intense.)
Serve a large spoonful or wedge of ricotta on a small plate. Spoon at least 2 tablespoons of rhubarb sauce over the cheese. Garnish with pine nuts or pistachio, if using.

ingredients: ¼ cup Brandy or Port, Sherry, or
2 cups Mixed, Fresh Berries or fruit
name: Sabayon
recipe: In a heatproof, medium-sized bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, sugar, vanilla, and brandy.
Set the bowl over gently simmering water and whisk constantly for 10 minutes or until the sauce triples in volume.
Pour the sauce over the berries and serve warm.
